- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often underestimates drop; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range or add lagged correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not continue rising; cap upward momentum at 0.5% above recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early days (first 5–7) and underestimates late days (last 5–7); apply “tail correction”: reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day in final 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply “mean reversion anchor” to forecast: center around 30-day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
